name: Drake Industrial Rivet-Grip Work Gloves
description:
Heavy-duty work gloves with rubberized palm coating and reinforced thumb saddles, built to survive daily use in construction, demolition, and salvage operations. The gloves feature a quick-release wrist strap that lets the wearer shed them in under a second — important when gloves get caught in machinery.

The most common work glove in GLMZ's lower tiers. They cost almost nothing, they last about three months of hard use, and they're available at every supply depot and street market in the city.
functionality: Grip enhancement, basic hand protection, emergency quick-release
what_it_says: You work with your hands every day and these gloves are as disposable as the work treats you.
story_hooks: Hundreds of discarded Rivet-Grip gloves are found piled outside an abandoned building — enough to account for a large workforce, but no construction permits were ever filed for the site.

physical_description.visual_profile: Chunky, utilitarian work gloves with a distinctly industrial silhouette. The hands look reinforced and capable, with pronounced padding at the palms and knuckles. The wrist section is structured and slightly flared. Overall impression is pure function over form — built for abuse, not aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Snug through the fingers and palm, with deliberate slack at the wrist to accommodate quick removal. The quick-release strap sits loose enough to disengage instantly but tight enough to stay secure during work. Designed for repeated donning/doffing with one hand.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy cotton canvas shell with reinforced synthetic leather palm panels. Rubberized grip coating applied to high-contact zones. The strap is friction-fit polymer that slides free under tension.
physical_description.texture: Rough, slightly textured canvas exterior. The rubberized palm is matte and tactile, designed to grip even wet or oily surfaces. Visible stitching throughout, with heavier thread at stress points. Worn edges show fraying typical of working conditions.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial gray-brown canvas with darker charcoal or black rubberized palms and thumb reinforcement. Minimal branding — small Drake Industrial tag stitched into the wrist seam. No decorative elements.
physical_description.closures: Quick-release friction-fit wrist strap that slides free with a sharp tug. No zippers, snaps, or buttons — designed for emergency one-handed removal.
distinctive_features: Reinforced thumb saddles (extra stitching and material at base of thumb)
Rubberized grip coating with micro-texture pattern
Double-thick padding at knuckles and palm heel
Small drainage grommets at the wrist
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Ubiquitous working-class standard. Affordable enough for daily replacement, durable enough to last a season.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals construction worker, salvage operative, demolition crew, or general manual laborer. Wearing Drake Rivet-Grips marks you as someone who works with their hands in the lower economic strata of GLMZ. Zero status aspirations — pure tool.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Palms show darkened wear patterns from sweat and grime. Canvas has frayed edges and small tears repaired with mismatched thread or not at all. Rubberized coating may be worn smooth in high-grip areas or partially peeling at the edges. Stains from oil, concrete dust, blood, and industrial sludge are normal.

image_prompt: Overhead flat-lay shot of weathered Drake Industrial Rivet-Grip work gloves on a grimy concrete surface, wrist strap splayed open in quick-release position. Harsh neon orange and cool blue shop lighting casting sharp shadows across the canvas. Close enough to see texture detail — worn rubberized palms with grip pattern visible, frayed edge of wrist strap, small tears and patch marks visible.
